name: Harding College

summary.text: Harding College (now Harding University) in Searcy, Arkansas, was led by president George S. Benson, who created the National Education Program to spread his free-enterprise 'Americanism' views. The program attracted donations to Harding including from Boeing and Gulf Oil, and the Alfred P. Sloan Foundation funded its animated free-enterprise films, which were shown in thousands of theatres under a deal with MGM.

facts.claim: The Encyclopedia of Arkansas says the National Education Program, founded by Harding president George S. Benson, attracted many donations to Harding, including from Boeing and Gulf Oil.
facts.quote: attracted many donations to Harding, including from Boeing and Gulf Oil

facts.claim: The National Film Preservation Foundation lists Harding's cartoons among the free-enterprise films funded by the Alfred P. Sloan Foundation; Benson's deal with MGM resulted in NEP-produced shorts being shown in 15,000 theaters.

connections.claim: Harding's president founded the NEP, which operated from the college.
connections.quote: founded by Harding College (now Harding University) president George S. Benson

openQuestions: Sources disagree on the NEP's founding date (1936, 1941 or 1948). The size of the Sloan Foundation grant is given as between $300,000 and $600,000 only in a tertiary summary. General Electric was not confirmed as a sponsor in any opened source.
